nodes.label: Weight Space Representation Learning via Neural Field Adaptation
nodes.author: Zhuoqian Yang, Mathieu Salzmann, Sabine Susstrunk

nodes.label: Multiplicative LoRA (mLoRA) for Neural Fields
nodes.rationale: Standard additive LoRA (W' = W + BA) introduces entanglement in neural fields by injecting new signal components into already-entangled feature mixtures. Multiplicative LoRA (W' = W ⊙ BA) instead scales existing features, preserving channel structure and avoiding further entanglement. This aligns with modulation mechanisms in generative neural fields and resolves internal permutation symmetry once external symmetry is broken by a shared base model.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Masking for Permutation Symmetry Breaking
nodes.rationale: Internal symmetry in LoRA factors (permuting r rank dimensions) is addressed by randomly freezing sqrt(d_out) entries per row of all A matrices; frozen positions are shared across instances and training runs, collapsing the GL(r)-fold equivalence class for each represented function. For mLoRA, frozen entries are zeroed out (removing rank components), which avoids weight entanglement unlike large-variance freezing in additive LoRA.

nodes.label: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs / Neural Fields)
nodes.rationale: INRs parameterize signals as continuous functions via neural networks, enabling resolution-independent, modality-agnostic representations. Using INR weights directly as data representations is motivated by their ability to encode diverse modalities in a unified architecture, but permutation symmetry of weights makes direct use challenging.

nodes.label: Diffusion Transformer on LoRA Weight Representations
nodes.rationale: A hierarchical LoRA layer encoder treats each rank component pair (a_i, b_i) as a token; vector-level positional encodings capture rank dimension indices and multi-head attention models intra-layer rank interactions; layer-level PE captures cross-layer relationships. This respects the paired structure of low-rank decomposition to enable generative modeling of weight spaces.

nodes.label: HyperDiffusion (Weight-Space Diffusion Baseline)
nodes.author: Erkon et al., 2023
nodes.rationale: HyperDiffusion trains a diffusion transformer over flattened MLP weights for implicit neural field generation; used as SOTA baseline in mLoRA experiments. mLoRA-Asym substantially outperforms HyperDiffusion on 2D FFHQ and 3D ShapeNet generation tasks.

nodes.label: Permutation Symmetry in Neural Network Weight Spaces
nodes.rationale: Functionally identical neural networks can occupy vastly different parameter space locations due to neuron reordering (permutation symmetry), making the weight distribution multi-modal and difficult to learn. External symmetries (from base neuron permutations) and internal symmetries (within LoRA rank dimensions) both require mitigation for effective weight space representation learning.

hyperedges.label: LoRA symmetry handling for weight-space generation
hyperedges.description: LoRA's GL_r symmetry and permutation symmetry are the core obstacles to using LoRA weights as data; multiplicative LoRA with asymmetric masking addresses both internal and external symmetries to produce structured, learnable weight spaces.
